newsitem.title: CHINA: China welcomes human rights decision by France.
newsitem.headline: China welcomes human rights decision by France.

text.p: China on Saturday welcomed a decision by France not to co-sponsor a U.N. motion criticising Beijing's human rights record, and slammed supporters of the resolution as trying to meddle in its internal affairs.

"China welcomes and appreciates France's decision that it will not participate this year in a United Nations human rights conference motion which will be directed against China's human rights conditions," the Xinhua news agency quoted a Foreign Ministry spokesman as saying.
Paris announced on Friday it would not co-sponsor a motion at the United Nations Human Rights Convention in Geneva, citing what it said was progress by China on fundamental freedoms.

The United States has said it plans to go ahead with the resolution, which has been put forward with the European Union every year since China crushed pro-democracy protests in Beijing's Tiananmen Square in June 1989.

"Their purpose of making anti-China motions is not a 'real concern' about human rights, but is to exert pressure on China and interfere in China's internal affairs under the pretext of human rights," the spokesman said.
China has so far escaped official censure by mustering support from developing nations, and the European Union is divided this year on whether to support the motion.
"We hope the other Western countries will reconsider their stance and refrain from making confrontation on the human rights issue," the spokesman said.
Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda told his Chinese counterpart in talks on Saturday that Tokyo was considering dropping its co-sponsorship of the motion.
